---
title: "Coefficient inference"
description: "Selected-support refits, standard errors and bootstrap selection stability."
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE,comment='#>',message=FALSE,warning=FALSE)
```

L0glm can report ordinary selected-model uncertainty, or repeat the fitting
pipeline under bootstrap resampling to assess variability and selection stability.
These optional calculations are requested in `summary()`.

## Selected-support standard errors

```{r conditional}
library(L0glm)
set.seed(51)
X <- matrix(rnorm(200*10),200,10)
y <- 1+2*X[,1]-2*X[,2]+rnorm(200)
fit <- l0glmFit(X,y,intercept=TRUE,lambda='gic',relaxed=TRUE)
details <- summary(fit,inference='conditional')
details$inference$coefficients
```

The selected coefficients are refitted without a sparsity penalty, with their
observation weights, offsets and coefficient constraints retained. The table
includes both the selected point estimates and the refitted estimates, standard
errors, intervals and Wald tests. The original fitted model is preserved.

Gaussian and other ordinary GLMs use model-based information; estimated scales
use selected-model Pearson dispersion. Negative binomial models retain fixed
shape or reestimate it as specified. Multinomial covariance is computed on its
selected zero-sum subspace and returned in CLR coordinates. Cox inference uses
weighted Breslow partial-likelihood information. Nonnegative boundaries and
singular information receive unavailable ordinary Wald standard errors.

The nominal fixed-model interpretation treats the chosen support as given.
When support recovery is reliable, it approaches the ordinary inference problem
with the correct model. Selection itself can add substantial uncertainty near
detection thresholds.

## Bootstrap selection stability

```{r bootstrap, eval=FALSE}
uncertainty <- summary(fit,inference='bootstrap',
  control.inference=list(nboot=199L,seed=1))
uncertainty$inference$coefficients
uncertainty$inference$diagnostics
```

Each replicate resamples observation rows and their weights and offsets, then
reruns the saved fit specification, including SIS/ISIS, interaction generation
and local support refinement. Starting exclusions remain fixed as specified.
Intervals include zero estimates when a coefficient is absent. Sparse draws and
selection frequencies retain every original predictor, with a shared union of
generated interaction terms. Failed fits, solver warnings, convergence and
timings are recorded.

A supplied seed preserves the caller's random-number state. The default memory
guard prevents large dense row-resampling blocks; `max.cells` can be set explicitly
when the required memory is available. Predictors are kept eligible throughout
the resampling procedure according to their original starting restrictions.

A model extracted from `l0glmTune()` retains its chosen penalty for this bootstrap.
A `refit` callback can repeat tuning within each replicate:

```{r retune, eval=FALSE}
retune <- function(args) {
  args$lambda <- NULL
  args$family <- gaussian()
  do.call(l0glmTune,c(args,list(tune='cv',nfolds=5L,nlambda=10L,
    plot=FALSE,printbest=FALSE)))$fit_best
}
uncertainty <- summary(fit,inference='bootstrap',
  control.inference=list(nboot=199L,seed=1,refit=retune))
```

Bootstrap intervals describe resampling variability. Near selection thresholds,
ordinary bootstrap and fixed-model intervals can have imperfect nominal coverage;
selection frequencies are useful stability diagnostics, rather than a proof that
the selected support is correct. See the
[reference page](../reference/coefficient_inference.html) for covariance formulas,
controls and the discussion by [Leeb and Poetscher (2008)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jeconom.2007.05.017).
